Beyond 'Click Here': Crafting Accessible Link Text for Everyone

2026-10-01 9 min read

Generic link text like 'click here' or 'read more' poses significant barriers for users relying on screen readers or those with cognitive disabilities. Learn how descriptive and unique link text not only improves accessibility but also enhances overall user experience and SEO.

Why Link Text Matters for Screen Reader and Keyboard Users

Links are the primary way people move through a website. While sighted visitors can glance at the paragraph around a 'Read more' link to guess where it goes, screen reader users frequently pull up a dedicated 'Elements List' or 'Links List' to jump directly to a destination without reading every word on the page.

When a page contains ten links all labeled 'Click here' or 'Learn more,' that links list becomes useless. Users have no idea which link opens pricing, which downloads a PDF, and which leads to a blog post.

WCAG Requirements for Link Purpose

  • WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) — Level A: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone, or from the link text together with its programmatically determined context.
  • WCAG 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only) — Level AAA: The purpose of each link can be identified from the link text alone, which is the best practice to aim for across navigation, cards, and body copy.

Practical Before-and-After Link Text Examples

<!-- Avoid -->
<p>To see our audit packages, <a href="pricing.html">click here</a>.</p>

<!-- Accessible -->
<p>Review our <a href="pricing.html">WCAG audit and remediation pricing</a>.</p>
<!-- Avoid in blog/product cards -->
<h3>WordPress Accessibility Fixes</h3>
<a href="wordpress-accessibility-fixes.html">Read more</a>

<!-- Accessible -->
<h3><a href="wordpress-accessibility-fixes.html">WordPress Accessibility Fixes</a></h3>
<p>Fix theme, plugin, and WooCommerce barriers.</p>

Best Practices for Special Link Types

  • Document downloads: Include the file type and size when helpful, such as 'Download the Accessibility Checklist (PDF, 420 KB)'.
  • External links opening in new tabs: Inform users when a link opens a new window or tab, and include rel="noopener noreferrer".
  • Skip links: Provide a 'Skip to main content' link at the top of every page so keyboard users can bypass repeated navigation menus.
  • Keep link text concise: Make the clickable phrase descriptive without wrapping an entire three-sentence paragraph in an <a> tag.
  • Distinguish links from buttons: Use <a href="..."> for navigation to another URL or section, and <button> for in-page actions like opening a modal or submitting a form.

How Accessible Link Text Also Improves SEO

Search engines use anchor text to understand what the linked page is about. Replacing 'click here' with descriptive phrases like 'manual WCAG accessibility audit' or 'ADA website compliance support' gives both assistive technologies and search crawlers clear, unambiguous signals.

How to Audit Your Links Today

Open NVDA (Insert + F7) or VoiceOver (Rotor -> Links) on your homepage and service pages. If any link in the list doesn't make sense on its own, rewrite it. For a broader check, try our free website accessibility self-check or request a manual review.
